days.title: Las palabras interrogativas
days.objective: Ask questions using qué, quién, dónde, cómo, cuándo, cuánto and por qué, and distinguish por qué from porque.
days.paretoFocus: Question words are the single most reusable structure for real conversation: without them you can't ask anything new.
drills: Write one question with each interrogative word.
Ask a partner 3 questions about their day using cómo, dónde and cuándo.
Answer a 'por qué' question with 'porque' three times.

items: Ask where the pharmacy is.
Ask how someone is.
Ask how many books there are.

activities.title: Qué, quién, dónde...
activities.intro: All interrogative words carry a written accent, which sets them apart from the unaccented connector que and from porque, 'because'.

items.en: How many books are there on the table?
items.note: cuánto agrees in gender and number with the noun that follows

items.hr: ¿Por qué estudias español? Porque es interesante.
items.en: Why do you study Spanish? Because it's interesting.
items.note: por qué (two words, accented) asks; porque (one word) answers

activities.title: Preguntar y responder
activities.intro: Practise the interrogative words and the por qué / porque contrast.

questions.prompt: 'Where do you live?' =
questions.explanation: dónde asks about location; vives is the tú form of vivir.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué palabra falta? '¿___ te llamas?'
questions.explanation: ¿Cómo te llamas? asks for a name.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿___ trabajas, por la mañana o por la tarde?
questions.explanation: cuándo asks about time in a general sense.

questions.prompt: Completa: La biblioteca ___ abierta los lunes. (estar)
questions.explanation: estar describes a current, changeable state.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Why do you study Spanish?'
questions.explanation: por qué, two words with an accent, opens the question.

activities.title: Preguntas nuevas
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. First contact between two new acquaintances using several interrogative words.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: My name is Diego. And you?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: My name is Marta. Where do you live?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vivo en Sevilla. ¿Y tú, dónde trabajas?
lines.en: I live in Seville. And you, where do you work?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Trabajo en un hospital. ¿Por qué estudias español?
lines.en: I work in a hospital. Why do you study Spanish?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Porque es interesante y útil para viajar.
lines.en: Because it's interesting and useful for travelling.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: How many languages do you speak?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: I speak two: Spanish and Portuguese.

days.title: La negación: no, nada, nadie, nunca
days.objective: Negate statements with no and use nada, nadie and nunca, including Spanish's required double negative.
days.paretoFocus: Negation is needed in nearly every conversation, and the Spanish double negative trips up English speakers who expect only one negative word.
drills: Negate 5 of your own sentences with no.
Write 3 sentences with nunca, nadie or nada.
Say aloud: 'No hay nadie aquí.'

items: Put no before a verb.
Say 'nobody comes' in Spanish.
Say you never study at night.

activities.title: No, nada, nadie, nunca
activities.intro: no goes right before the verb. When nada, nadie or nunca come after the verb, Spanish also keeps the no, unlike English's single negative.

items.hr: No hay nadie en la clase.
items.en: There is nobody in the class.
items.note: no + hay + nadie: the double negative is obligatory
nunca before the verb needs no extra no

items.hr: No tengo nada en la mochila.
items.en: I don't have anything in my backpack.

items.hr: No viene nadie a la fiesta.
items.en: Nobody is coming to the party.

activities.title: Nada, nadie, nunca
activities.intro: Practise negation and the double negative.

questions.prompt: 'I never eat fish' =
questions.explanation: nunca before the verb needs no extra no.

questions.prompt: Completa: 'No hay ___ en la nevera.' ('anything')
questions.explanation: nada = 'anything/nothing' as a direct object; it pairs with no.

questions.prompt: Completa: Nunca ___ el periódico por la mañana. (yo, leer)
questions.explanation: leer is a regular -er verb: leo in the yo form.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ tengo hermanos. (negative form)
questions.explanation: no immediately precedes the conjugated verb to negate a sentence.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Nobody is coming to the party.'
questions.explanation: nadie after the verb still requires no before it.

activities.title: La fiesta sorpresa
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A conversation about a party that isn't going well, full of negation.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, no está nadie. Todos trabajan hoy.
lines.en: No, nobody's here. Everyone is working today.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Are they never free in the afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, nunca están libres. Siempre estudian o trabajan.
lines.en: No, they're never free. They always study or work.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Hay algo de comer en la fiesta?
lines.en: Is there anything to eat at the party?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, no hay nada. No hay comida ni bebida.
lines.en: No, there's nothing. There's no food or drink.

days.title: Los números 0 a 20 y la edad
days.objective: Count from 0 to 20 and say your age using tener.
days.paretoFocus: Age and basic numbers come up in nearly every first conversation and every form you'll ever fill in.
drills: Count aloud from 0 to 20.
Say your age and the age of two people you know.
Write the numbers 11 to 20 from memory.

items: Say the numbers 1 to 10.
Ask someone's age.
Conjugate tener for yo and tú.

activities.title: Tener años
activities.intro: The numbers 0-20 are largely irregular and must be memorized individually. Age uses tener, not ser, plus the number and años.

items.hr: cero, uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco
items.en: zero, one, two, three, four, five

items.note: dieciséis carries a written accent; the rest of the teens do not
tener + number + años, never ser, for age
tienes is the tú form of tener

items.en: My sister is ten years old.
items.note: tiene is the él/ella/usted form

items.en: We have a dog at home.
items.note: tenemos is the nosotros form
tenéis is the vosotros form, used in Spain for an informal plural you

items.hr: Mis padres tienen un coche nuevo.
items.en: My parents have a new car.
items.note: tienen is the ellos/ellas/ustedes form

activities.title: Números y edad
activities.intro: Practise counting and stating age.

questions.prompt: 'I am fifteen years old' =
questions.explanation: Age is always tener + number + años.

questions.prompt: ¿Cómo se escribe 16?
questions.explanation: Written as one word, with an accent on the e.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ana ___ doce años. (tener)
questions.explanation: tercera persona singular de tener: tiene.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ veinte estudiantes en la clase. (haber)
questions.explanation: hay is invariable no matter what number follows it.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'How old are you?'
questions.explanation: Literally 'how many years do you have.'

activities.title: ¿Cuántos años tienes?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two people compare ages and family.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: I'm twenty. Do you have siblings?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, tengo un hermano. Tiene quince años.
lines.en: Yes, I have a brother. He's fifteen.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: He's very young! Is he a student?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, es estudiante y hay veinte alumnos en la clase.
lines.en: Yes, he's a student, and there are twenty pupils in the class.

days.title: Los números 21 a 100 y el precio
days.objective: Count from 21 to 100 and ask and understand a price in euros.
days.paretoFocus: Prices come up in every shop, market and menu; this is the numeral range you'll use most in transactions.
drills: Count by tens from 20 to 100.
Say 3 prices aloud in euros.
Ask how much something costs.

items: Say the number 21.
Say the number 100.
Ask the price of a coffee.

activities.title: Veintiuno a cien
activities.intro: 21-29 fuse into one word (veintiuno...), but from 31 the decade and unit separate: treinta y uno. cien stands alone; ciento comes before another number.

items.note: 21-29 are one word; 30 stands alone

items.hr: treinta y uno, treinta y dos
items.note: from 31 the parts separate: decade + y + unit

items.hr: cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta, setenta, ochenta, noventa, cien
items.en: forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, a hundred

items.note: asks for a total, answered with ser

items.en: How much does the coffee cost?
items.note: cuesta is a fixed, memorized form here; its full pattern comes later in the course

activities.title: El precio
activities.intro: Practise larger numbers and asking a price.

questions.prompt: 'Fifty-five' =
questions.explanation: From 30 upward: decade + y + unit, as three separate words.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la pregunta correcta para pedir el precio?
questions.explanation: cuánto asks about quantity or price.

questions.prompt: Completa: El billete cuesta treinta y cinco ___. (currency unit)
questions.explanation: euros is the currency; céntimos names the smaller unit.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿___ una farmacia por aquí? (haber)
questions.explanation: New, unspecified information uses hay.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'How much does the ticket cost?'
questions.explanation: cuánto + cuesta + the item, as a fixed question pattern.

activities.title: En la tienda
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Buying a couple of small items and totalling the price.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Good morning. What do you need?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Hello. How much does the pen cost?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Cuesta un euro con veinte céntimos.
lines.en: It costs one euro twenty cents.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Entonces son tres euros con veinte céntimos en total, ¿no?
lines.en: So that's three euros twenty cents in total, right?

days.title: La familia
days.objective: Name close family members and talk about who is in your family using ser, estar, hay and tener.
days.paretoFocus: Family is one of the first topics in any real conversation and recycles four verbs the learner already knows.
drills: Draw your family tree and label it in Spanish.
Say 3 sentences about your family with tener.
Say where two family members are with estar.

items: Name 5 family words.
Say 'I have two brothers.'
Say a profession without an article.

activities.title: La familia
activities.intro: Most family nouns pair by the already known -o/-a gender pattern; a few, like padre/madre, change the root entirely.

items.hr: el padre, la madre, los padres
items.en: the father, the mother, the parents
items.note: los padres also means 'the parents' as a pair

items.hr: el hijo, la hija, los hijos
items.en: the son, the daughter, the children

items.hr: el abuelo, la abuela; el marido, la mujer
items.en: the grandfather, the grandmother; the husband, the wife

activities.title: La familia
activities.intro: Practise family vocabulary.

questions.prompt: 'The grandmother' =
questions.explanation: Feminine noun, feminine article: la abuela.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué palabra significa 'wife'?
questions.explanation: mujer means both 'woman' and 'wife' depending on context.

questions.prompt: Completa: Tengo dos hermanos y una ___. (sister)
questions.explanation: hermana is the feminine counterpart of hermano.

questions.prompt: Completa: Soy ___ médico muy conocido. (the article that returns once an adjective is added)
questions.explanation: The article returns once the profession carries an adjective.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I have three children.'
questions.explanation: hijos covers a mixed or all-male group of children.

activities.title: La familia de Marta
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Comparing family size and asking about grandparents.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: How many siblings do you have?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tengo un hermano y una hermana. ¿Y tú?
lines.en: I have one brother and one sister. And you?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo no tengo hermanos, soy hija única. ¿Viven los abuelos cerca de aquí?
lines.en: I don't have siblings, I'm an only child. Do your grandparents live nearby?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, la abuela vive en Sevilla. Tiene setenta años.
lines.en: Yes, grandma lives in Seville. She's seventy.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, el abuelo no trabaja. Está en casa con la abuela.
lines.en: No, grandpa doesn't work. He's at home with grandma.

days.title: Los posesivos: mi, tu, su, nuestro, vuestro
days.objective: Use possessive adjectives that agree with the thing owned, not the owner, and resolve the ambiguity of su.
days.paretoFocus: Possessives are needed to talk about anyone's family, belongings or plans, and su's ambiguity is a genuine trap for beginners.
drills: Say 5 things using mi/tu/su.
Make 3 sentences with nuestro/nuestra agreeing correctly.
Rewrite 2 ambiguous su sentences with de él or de ella.

items: Say 'my brother' and 'my sister'.
Say 'our house'.
Clarify whose book it is with de ella.

activities.title: Mi, tu, su...
activities.intro: Spanish possessives agree with the noun they modify, not with the owner: nuestro changes for gender and number, but mi/tu/su only change for number.

items.hr: Mi hermano y mis hermanas viven aquí.
items.en: My brother and my sisters live here.
items.note: mi/mis: only number changes
su is ambiguous; Spanish clarifies with de él, de ella or de ellos

items.hr: Es la casa de ella, no de él.
Nuestra familia es pequeña y vuestro piso es grande.
items.en: Our family is small and your (plural) flat is big.
items.note: nuestro/vuestro agree in gender and number

activities.title: Los posesivos
activities.intro: Practise possessive agreement and resolving su.

questions.prompt: 'Our car' =
questions.explanation: coche is masculine singular, so nuestro agrees.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase resuelve la ambigüedad de 'su libro'?
questions.explanation: de él/de ella replaces the ambiguous su when the owner needs to be clear.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿Dónde están ___ padres, Juan?
questions.explanation: tus agrees with the plural padres, for a tú owner.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿___ vive tu hermano, en Madrid o en Sevilla?
questions.explanation: dónde asks about location.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'His house is big.'
questions.explanation: su covers his/her/their; grande does not change for gender.

activities.title: ¿De quién es esto?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Sorting out whose things are whose.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, no es mi bolígrafo. Es de Marta.
lines.en: No, it's not my pen. It's Marta's.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es nuestra. Mi hermana y yo usamos esa mochila.
lines.en: It's ours. My sister and I use that backpack.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, nuestra casa está muy cerca del colegio.
lines.en: Yes, our house is very near the school.

days.title: Este, ese, aquel: los demostrativos
days.objective: Point out things at three distances with este, ese and aquel and their full agreement forms.
days.paretoFocus: Demonstratives are constant in speech, pointing at objects in shops, on tables, and across a room.
drills: Point at 3 objects near you using este/esta.
Point at something across the room using aquel/aquella.
Say one sentence with ese for something near the listener.

items: Say 'this book' and 'that pen'.
Say 'those chairs over there'.
Explain the three distances in your own words.

activities.title: Este, ese, aquel
activities.intro: Spanish marks three distances: este for near the speaker, ese for near the listener, aquel for far from both. All forms agree with the noun in gender and number.

items.en: Those mountains over there are tall.
Is it this one or that one?

items.hr: Estos zapatos son cómodos, esos no.
items.en: These shoes are comfortable, those aren't.
items.note: estos/esos: masculine plural forms

activities.title: Los demostrativos
activities.intro: Practise the three distances.

questions.prompt: 'These flowers' (near me) =
questions.explanation: flores is feminine plural, near the speaker: estas.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué demostrativo señala algo lejos de los dos hablantes?
questions.explanation: aquel marks distance from both speaker and listener.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ silla, aquí a mi lado, está libre.
questions.explanation: esta agrees with silla (feminine) and marks nearness to the speaker.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ hay nadie en aquella sala.
questions.explanation: no negates the sentence before hay.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Those shoes over there are expensive.'
questions.explanation: aquellos marks distance; caros agrees in gender and number.

activities.title: En el mercado
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Choosing fruit at three different distances.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, esta fruta es muy buena. ¿Y esas manzanas?
lines.en: Yes, this fruit is very good. And those apples?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Esas son de aquí, pero aquellas naranjas son de otra región.
lines.en: Those are from here, but those oranges over there are from another region.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: How much do these apples cost?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: They cost two euros a kilo.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, un kilo de estas y medio kilo de aquellas naranjas, por favor.
lines.en: Okay, a kilo of these and half a kilo of those oranges, please.

days.title: Describir a una persona
days.objective: Describe someone's appearance and character using ser + adjective and tener + noun.
days.paretoFocus: Physical and character description is constant in everyday talk about family, friends and strangers, and it recycles ser, estar and tener together.
drills: Describe a friend's appearance in 3 sentences.
Describe a friend's character in 3 sentences.
Say what colour someone's eyes and hair are.

items: Say 'she is tall' and 'he is short'.
Say 'he has long hair'.
Name 3 character adjectives.

activities.title: Describir a alguien
activities.intro: ser + adjective describes lasting qualities like height or kindness; tener + noun describes physical features like hair and eyes, which Spanish treats as things you 'have', not things you 'are'.

items.note: -ita is a common affectionate diminutive

items.hr: Tiene el pelo largo y los ojos verdes.
items.en: She has long hair and green eyes.
items.note: tener + noun for physical features, unlike English 'to be'

items.hr: Es muy simpático pero un poco tímido.
items.en: He is very nice but a bit shy.

activities.title: Descripciones
activities.intro: Practise ser and tener for description.

questions.prompt: 'He has blue eyes' =
questions.explanation: Physical features use tener, not ser, plus the definite article.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué adjetivo describe el carácter, no el físico?
questions.explanation: generoso describes personality; the others describe appearance.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi abuela ___ el pelo blanco. (tener)
questions.explanation: tercera persona singular: tiene.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi hermano ___ dieciocho años y es muy alto. (tener)
questions.explanation: tener also states age.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'She is hardworking and has short hair.'
questions.explanation: Two structures combine: ser for character, tener for the feature.

activities.title: ¿Cómo es?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Describing a sister's looks and character.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es bajita, morena y tiene los ojos marrones.
lines.en: She's short, dark-haired, and has brown eyes.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es muy simpática y trabajadora, pero un poco tímida.
lines.en: She's very nice and hardworking, but a bit shy.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, mi madre es alta y rubia. Son muy diferentes.
lines.en: No, my mother is tall and blonde. They're very different.

days.title: Verbos con cambio e > ie
days.objective: Conjugate and use e>ie stem-changing verbs like querer, empezar, preferir, entender and pensar.
days.paretoFocus: This is the first of the four irregular families that make up most of Spanish's 'irregular' verbs; the pattern generalises to hundreds of verbs once learned.
drills: Conjugate querer in full.
Say 3 things you prefer using preferir.
Say when class starts using empezar.

items: Say the nosotros form of querer.
Say 'I want' and 'you want'.
Explain why nosotros keeps the e.

activities.title: La bota: e > ie
activities.intro: In these verbs the stem vowel e becomes ie wherever the stress falls on the stem, which is every form except nosotros and vosotros. Drawing a line around those four changed forms makes a boot shape, so linguists call this the boot verb pattern.

items.hr: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren
items.en: I want, you want, he/she/you want, we want, you (pl.) want, they/you want
items.note: the boot: nosotros and vosotros keep quer-, the rest change to quier-

items.hr: Preferimos el café, no el té.
Pienso que es una buena idea.
items.en: I think it's a good idea.
items.note: pienso que introduces an opinion, the same pattern as creo que

activities.title: Querer, empezar, preferir...
activities.intro: Practise the e to ie boot pattern.

questions.prompt: 'We understand' =
questions.explanation: nosotros keeps the plain stem: entendemos, no stem change.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué forma es correcta para 'tú'?
questions.explanation: tú changes the stem: quieres, with the regular -es ending.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ellos ___ empezar a las ocho. (preferir)
questions.explanation: ellos changes the stem: prefieren.

questions.prompt: Completa: El billete de tren ___ treinta euros.
questions.explanation: cuesta, already memorized from an earlier lesson; its full pattern arrives soon.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I think it's a good idea.'
questions.explanation: pensar stem-changes to pienso; que introduces what you think.

activities.title: Planes para hoy
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two colleagues compare work schedules and drink preferences.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: What time do you start work?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: I start at nine. And you?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo empiezo más tarde. ¿Qué prefieres, café o té?
lines.en: I start later. What do you prefer, coffee or tea?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: I prefer coffee. Do you understand why?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, pienso que el café es bueno por la mañana.
lines.en: Yes, I think coffee is good in the morning.

days.title: Verbos con cambio o > ue
days.objective: Conjugate and use o>ue stem-changing verbs like poder, volver, dormir, encontrar, costar and jugar.
days.paretoFocus: The same boot pattern as e>ie, now with o to ue, covers another large group of everyday verbs including the ability verb poder.
drills: Conjugate poder in full.
Say what time you get home using volver.
Say what game you play using jugar.

items: Say 'I can' and 'we can'.
Say the nosotros form of dormir.
Explain why jugar changes u, not o.

activities.title: La bota: o > ue
activities.intro: Same boot shape as e>ie, but the stem vowel o becomes ue in every form except nosotros and vosotros. jugar is the one verb in this family that starts from u instead of o, but it follows exactly the same pattern: u becomes ue.

items.hr: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden
items.en: I can, you can, he/she/you can, we can, you (pl.) can, they/you can
What time do you get back home?

items.hr: Juego al fútbol por la tarde.
items.en: I play football in the afternoon.
items.note: al is a fixed contraction (a + el) used here as a set phrase; the full rule arrives in a later lesson

activities.title: Poder, volver, dormir...
activities.intro: Practise the o to ue boot pattern.

questions.prompt: 'They can come' =
questions.explanation: ellos/ellas/ustedes changes the stem: pueden.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué forma usa 'nosotros' sin cambio de raíz?
questions.explanation: nosotros always keeps the plain stem: dormimos, not duermimos.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿___ ayudar con esto? (tú, poder)
questions.explanation: tú changes the stem: puedes.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi abuelo no ___ dormir bien por la noche. (poder)
questions.explanation: tercera persona: puede.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I can't find my keys.'
questions.explanation: encontrar stem-changes to encuentro in the yo form.

activities.title: Un día libre
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. A tired friend cancels football plans and loses their keys.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Can you play football this afternoon?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No puedo. Duermo poco y estoy cansado.
lines.en: I can't. I sleep little and I'm tired.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿A qué hora vuelves del trabajo cada día?
lines.en: What time do you get back from work each day?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vuelvo a las seis, pero hoy no encuentro mis llaves y estoy nervioso.
lines.en: I get back at six, but today I can't find my keys and I'm nervous.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Yes, thanks. We can look together.

days.title: Verbos con cambio e > i
days.objective: Conjugate and use the e>i stem-changing verbs pedir, seguir, repetir and servir.
days.paretoFocus: This smaller family is easy to confuse with e>ie; keeping them separate matters for ordering food and following directions correctly.
drills: Conjugate pedir in full.
Say what you usually order at a café using pedir.
Say which street to follow using seguir.

items: Say 'I order' and 'we order'.
Explain why e > i differs from e > ie.
Say 'he follows the same route'.

activities.title: La bota: e > i
activities.intro: A third stem-change pattern, only for -ir verbs: e simplifies to i in the same boot positions as before, everywhere except nosotros and vosotros.

items.hr: pido, pides, pide, pedimos, pedís, piden
items.en: I order/ask for, you order, he/she/you order, we order, you (pl.) order, they/you order

items.hr: Sigo todo recto y luego giro a la izquierda.
items.en: I go straight ahead and then turn left.

items.hr: Repetimos la lección todos los días.
items.en: We repeat the lesson every day.
items.note: nosotros keeps the plain stem: repetimos

activities.title: Pedir, seguir, servir...
activities.intro: Practise the e to i boot pattern.

questions.prompt: 'They order' =
questions.explanation: ellos changes the stem: piden.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué forma corresponde a 'nosotros' con servir?
questions.explanation: nosotros keeps the plain stem: servimos.

questions.prompt: Completa: Yo siempre ___ agua con la comida. (pedir)
questions.explanation: yo changes the stem: pido.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ camarero siempre repite el pedido. (our)
questions.explanation: nuestro agrees with camarero, masculine singular.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'What do you order here?'
questions.explanation: pides is the tú form of pedir, with the e to i change.

activities.title: En el restaurante
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Ordering food and commenting on the service.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: I order fish, and you, what do you order?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Pido carne. El camarero siempre sirve rápido aquí.
lines.en: I order meat. The waiter always serves quickly here.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Es verdad. Nunca repite el pedido dos veces.
lines.en: It's true. He never repeats the order twice.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Do we stay here or look for another place?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Seguimos aquí, la comida es buena.
lines.en: Let's stay here, the food is good.

days.title: Los irregulares en yo
days.objective: Use verbs that are irregular only in the yo form: hacer, poner, salir, traer, saber, ver, dar and conocer.
days.paretoFocus: These are some of the most frequent verbs in the language, and the irregularity is confined to a single form, which makes them fast to learn.
drills: Say 5 sentences, one for each yo-form irregular verb.
Say what you know how to do using sé.
Say what time you go out using salir.

items: Say 'I do' and 'I put'.
Say 'I know' (a fact) using saber.
Say the tú form of hacer, which is regular.

activities.title: Irregulares en yo
activities.intro: hago, pongo, salgo, traigo, sé, veo, doy and conozco are the only irregular forms in each of these verbs; every other person is perfectly regular.

items.hr: Hago la comida y pongo la mesa.
items.en: I make the food and I set the table.

items.hr: Salgo de casa a las ocho.
Traigo el pan para la cena.
items.en: I bring the bread for dinner.

items.hr: Sé cocinar, pero no sé conducir.
items.en: I know how to cook, but I don't know how to drive.
items.note: saber + infinitive: knowing how to do something

items.hr: Veo la tele y conozco bien el barrio.
items.en: I watch TV and I know the neighbourhood well.
items.note: conocer: to know a person or place, different from saber

activities.title: Hago, pongo, salgo...
activities.intro: Practise the yo-form irregular verbs.

questions.prompt: 'I know how to swim' =
questions.explanation: saber + infinitive expresses knowing how; the yo form is sé, with an accent.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué verbo corresponde a 'to know a person'?
questions.explanation: conocer is for people and places; saber is for facts and skills.

questions.prompt: Completa: Yo ___ la mesa para la cena. (poner)
questions.explanation: yo form: pongo, irregular only here.

questions.prompt: Completa: Traigo ___ libros para la clase de mañana. (these)
questions.explanation: estos points to something near the speaker.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I leave home at eight and I bring the bread.'
questions.explanation: salgo and traigo are both irregular only in the yo form.

activities.title: La rutina de la mañana
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Comparing morning routines.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: What time do you leave home?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: I leave at seven. And you?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Yo salgo más tarde. ¿Qué haces por la mañana?
lines.en: I leave later. What do you do in the morning?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Hago café, pongo la mesa y traigo el periódico.
lines.en: I make coffee, set the table and bring the newspaper.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Do you know how to cook well?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sé cocinar cosas sencillas. No sé hacer postres.
lines.en: I know how to cook simple things. I don't know how to make desserts.

days.title: Ir, y el destino con a
days.objective: Conjugate ir and say where you are going, using the contraction al.
days.paretoFocus: ir carries more weight than almost any other verb here: it is irregular, it is the base of the near future taught next, and its contraction al is obligatory rather than optional.
drills: Conjugate ir in full.
Say 3 places you go regularly.
Practise al versus a la with 3 different places.

items: Say 'I go' and 'we go'.
Say 'to the park' using al.
Say 'to the library' using a la.

activities.title: Ir a un lugar
activities.intro: ir is irregular in every form: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. Before el, the preposition a always contracts to al; before la, it stays separate as a la.

items.hr: Voy al parque todos los días.
items.en: I go to the park every day.
items.note: a + el = al, always contracted, never a el

items.hr: Vamos a la playa en verano.
items.en: We go to the beach in summer.
Are you going to the doctor today?
They go to school on foot.

items.note: no article before casa de + name

activities.title: Ir y la contracción al
activities.intro: Practise ir and the al contraction.

questions.prompt: 'We go to the park' =
questions.explanation: a + el always contracts to al.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué forma corresponde a 'ellos' con ir?
questions.explanation: ir is fully irregular: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van.

questions.prompt: Completa: ¿___ a la fiesta esta noche? (tú, ir)
questions.explanation: tú form: vas.

questions.prompt: Completa: La chica alta y rubia ___ a mi colegio también. (ir)
questions.explanation: tercera persona: va.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Are you going to the doctor today?'
questions.explanation: al is obligatory before médico, masculine.

activities.title: ¿Adónde vas?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Two friends heading to different places, then deciding to walk together.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy al mercado. ¿Y tú, adónde vas?
lines.en: I'm going to the market. And you, where are you going?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Voy a la biblioteca. ¿Vamos juntos hasta allí?
lines.en: I'm going to the library. Shall we go together that far?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, vamos. Luego voy al mercado yo sola.
lines.en: Okay, let's go. Then I'll go to the market by myself.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Does your sister also go to the market?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: No, ella va al gimnasio por la tarde.
lines.en: No, she goes to the gym in the afternoon.

days.title: Ir a + infinitivo: el futuro próximo
days.objective: Talk about what you are going to do using ir a + infinitive, the only future structure taught at this level.
days.paretoFocus: This periphrasis is the everyday spoken way to talk about the future across the whole Spanish-speaking world, more common in speech than the -ré future.
drills: Say 3 plans for tomorrow using ir a.
Make one of your plans negative.
Ask a partner what they are going to do this weekend.

items: Conjugate ir a comer for yo and nosotros.
Negate a plan with ir a.
Say 'they are going to travel'.

activities.title: Ir a + infinitivo
activities.intro: Present of ir + a + an infinitive expresses a plan or intention, exactly like English 'going to'. Across the whole Spanish-speaking world this is the everyday spoken future; the -ré ending exists but is far less common in speech.

items.en: I'm going to study this afternoon.
Are you going to come to the party?
We're not going to work tomorrow.
items.note: no goes before va/vamos, not before the infinitive

items.en: They're going to travel to Seville.

activities.title: Ir a + infinitivo
activities.intro: Practise the near future.

questions.prompt: 'I'm going to eat' =
questions.explanation: ir (present) + a + infinitive, no gerund or participle.

questions.prompt: ¿Dónde va 'no' en la negación de ir a?
questions.explanation: no negates the conjugated form of ir, not the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Completa: Ellos ___ a comprar pan. (ir)
questions.explanation: tercera persona plural: van.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mañana ___ empezar un curso nuevo. (ir a, yo)
questions.explanation: voy a + infinitive states a plan.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It's going to rain tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: va (from ir) + a + llover; llover only exists in the third person.

activities.title: Planes para el fin de semana
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Weekend plans, one busy and one relaxed.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
lines.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Voy a visitar a mis abuelos. ¿Y tú?
lines.en: I'm going to visit my grandparents. And you?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Voy a descansar en casa. No voy a salir mucho.
lines.en: I'm going to rest at home. I'm not going to go out much.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Are you (plural) going to do anything special?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: No, vamos a dormir mucho y a ver películas.
lines.en: No, we're going to sleep a lot and watch movies.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Suena muy tranquilo. Yo también voy a descansar el domingo.
lines.en: That sounds very relaxing. I'm also going to rest on Sunday.

days.title: Gustar: el verbo que funciona al revés
days.objective: Use gustar correctly by treating the thing liked as the grammatical subject, with me/te/le/nos/os/les marking who likes it.
days.paretoFocus: gustar is the construction English speakers get most wrong because they translate 'to like' directly; understanding the backwards logic prevents that error permanently.
drills: Say 3 things you like using me gusta or me gustan.
Say one thing you don't like.
Ask a partner what they like using te gusta.

items: Explain why gustar has only two common forms.
Say 'I like books' with the correct form.
Say 'we like the city'.

activities.title: Me gusta, me gustan
activities.intro: Gustar flips the usual sentence around: the thing being liked acts as the subject of the verb, while the person who likes it appears as a short pronoun in front of it, me, te or le for one person, nos, os or les for more than one. Because the subject is almost always a thing rather than a person, gustar mostly shows up in just two forms in practice, gusta for one liked thing and gustan for several.

items.note: el café is the subject; gusta agrees with it, singular
los libros is plural, so the verb is gustan
an infinitive after gustar is always singular: gusta, never gustan

items.hr: Nos gustan las playas, pero no nos gusta el frío.
items.en: We like beaches, but we don't like the cold.

activities.title: Gustar
activities.intro: Practise gustar agreement.

questions.prompt: 'I like apples' =
questions.explanation: manzanas is plural, so gustar agrees: gustan.

questions.prompt: ¿Por qué 'gusta' y no 'gustan' en 'Le gusta bailar'?
options: porque un infinitivo siempre es singular
porque bailar es un sustantivo plural
no hay razón, las dos son correctas
questions.answer: porque un infinitivo siempre es singular
questions.explanation: An infinitive as the thing liked always takes the singular gusta.

questions.prompt: Completa: A nosotros nos ___ el cine. (gustar, singular)
questions.explanation: el cine is singular, so gusta agrees.

questions.prompt: Completa: A ella le gustan los deportes, pero no ___ dormir mucho. (poder)
questions.explanation: poder stem-changes to puede.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'We like beaches.'
questions.explanation: playas is plural, so gustar takes the -n form: gustan.

activities.title: Gustos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Comparing tastes in cinema and books.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, me gusta mucho. ¿Y a ti te gustan los libros?
lines.en: Yes, I like it a lot. And do you like books?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, me gustan mucho las novelas. No me gusta el teatro.
lines.en: Yes, I like novels a lot. I don't like theatre.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A mí sí me gusta el teatro.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Qué te gusta hacer los fines de semana?
lines.en: What do you like to do on weekends?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Me gusta leer y me gustan los paseos por el parque.
lines.en: I like reading and I like walks in the park.

days.title: Gustar con a mí, a ti... y también / tampoco
days.objective: Add emphasis or clarity to gustar with a mí, a ti, a Ana, and agree or disagree using también and tampoco.
days.paretoFocus: Real conversations about preferences constantly need to clarify whose opinion you mean and to agree or disagree quickly, which is exactly what this lesson adds.
drills: Say what you like with a mí for emphasis.
Agree with someone's like using también.
Agree with someone's dislike using tampoco.

items: Say 'me too' after a positive statement.
Say 'me neither' after a negative statement.
Clarify 'a Ana le gusta' out loud.

activities.title: A mí, a ti... también, tampoco
activities.intro: These forms add emphasis or resolve an ambiguous le: a ti, a mí, a él, a ella, a Ana and so on can be placed before me/te/le so the listener knows exactly who is meant. To agree with a positive statement, tack on también ('me too'); to agree with a negative one, use tampoco ('me neither').

items.hr: A mí me gusta el café, pero a mi hermano no.
items.en: I like coffee, but my brother doesn't.

items.note: a Ana clarifies who le refers to

items.hr: Me gusta el jazz. A mí también.
No me gusta madrugar. A mí tampoco.
items.en: I don't like getting up early. Me neither.

items.hr: A vosotros os gustan los deportes, ¿verdad?

activities.title: También y tampoco
activities.intro: Practise agreeing and disagreeing about preferences.

questions.prompt: Alguien dice 'Me gusta el chocolate' y tú estás de acuerdo:
questions.explanation: también agrees with a positive statement.

questions.prompt: Alguien dice 'No me gusta el pescado' y tú estás de acuerdo:
questions.explanation: tampoco agrees with a negative statement.

questions.prompt: Completa: ___ Marta le gustan los gatos. (clarificación con a)
questions.explanation: a + name clarifies who le refers to.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mis amigos siempre ___ pescado en el restaurante. (pedir)
questions.explanation: pedir stem-changes to piden in the third person plural.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Ana likes to swim, and I like it too.'
questions.explanation: a Ana clarifies le; a mí también agrees.

activities.title: Gustos compartidos
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Comparing sport preferences with a friend and their sister.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A mí me gusta mucho el deporte. ¿Y a ti?
lines.en: I like sport a lot. And you?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A mí también. Me gusta correr por la mañana.
lines.en: Me too. I like running in the morning.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: A mi hermana no le gusta correr, prefiere nadar.
lines.en: My sister doesn't like running, she prefers swimming.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: A mí tampoco me gusta mucho correr en invierno.
lines.en: I don't like running much in winter either.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: ¿Os gustan los deportes de equipo, a ti y a tus amigos?
lines.en: Do you and your friends like team sports?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, nos gustan mucho, sobre todo el fútbol.
lines.en: Yes, we like them a lot, especially football.

days.title: Querer y poder + infinitivo
days.objective: Combine querer and poder with an infinitive to express wants and ability, and ask for permission with ¿Puedo...?
days.paretoFocus: These two verbs plus an infinitive cover most everyday requests and offers without needing the imperative at all.
drills: Say 3 things you want to do using querer + infinitive.
Ask permission for 3 things using ¿Puedo...?
Say something you can't do using no puedo.

items: Say 'I want to eat'.
Ask 'Can I open the window?'
Say 'I can't come today'.

activities.title: Querer y poder + infinitivo
activities.intro: querer and poder, already known as e>ie and o>ue stem-changers, combine directly with an infinitive to say what you want to do or are able to do. ¿Puedo...? is the standard polite way to ask permission, with no imperative needed.

items.en: I want to learn Spanish well.

items.note: ¿Puedo...? is the standard polite way to ask permission

items.en: Do you want to come with us?
We want to rest a little.

activities.title: Querer, poder y el permiso
activities.intro: Practise asking for permission and stating wants.

questions.prompt: 'Can I come in?' =
questions.explanation: poder + infinitive asks permission; the yo form is puedo, and the question needs a question mark.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál de estas frases pide permiso para entrar?
questions.explanation: poder + infinitive in a question is how Spanish asks permission. Quiero and necesito state a wish or a need without asking for anything, and entro ahora simply reports what you are doing.

questions.prompt: Completa: Nosotros ___ viajar este verano. (querer)
questions.explanation: nosotros keeps the plain stem: queremos.

questions.prompt: Completa: Quiero salir, pero primero ___ la mesa. (poner, yo)
questions.explanation: pongo is irregular only in the yo form.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'Can I open the window?'
questions.explanation: ¿Puedo + infinitivo? is the standard way to ask permission.

activities.title: ¿Puedo...?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Asking permission and offering help with an exercise.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Can I come in for a moment?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Yes, of course. What do you want?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Tengo una pregunta. ¿Puedes ayudar con este ejercicio?
lines.en: I have a question. Can you help with this exercise?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: Of course I can. Do you want to start now?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Sí, pero antes, ¿puedo abrir la ventana? Hace calor.
lines.en: Yes, but first, can I open the window? It's hot.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, claro, puedes abrir la ventana.
lines.en: Yes, of course, you can open the window.

days.title: Tener que y hay que + infinitivo
days.objective: Express personal obligation with tener que and general or impersonal obligation with hay que.
days.paretoFocus: Obligation is unavoidable in daily life, and the personal/impersonal split, who exactly must do it versus a general rule, is a genuine distinction English doesn't mark the same way.
drills: Say 3 things you have to do today using tener que.
Say 1 general rule using hay que.
Contrast a personal and an impersonal obligation on the same topic.

items: Say 'I have to work tomorrow'.
Say a general rule with hay que.
Explain the difference between tener que and hay que.

activities.title: Tener que y hay que
activities.intro: tener que + infinitive names who must do something, since tener is conjugated for each person: tengo que, tienes que. hay que + infinitive states a general obligation with no named subject at all, since hay is invariable.

items.en: You have to arrive on time.
One has to respect the rules.
items.note: hay que: no specific person named, a general rule for everyone

items.hr: Para aprobar, hay que estudiar mucho.
items.en: To pass, one has to study a lot.

activities.title: Obligación personal e impersonal
activities.intro: Practise tener que and hay que.

questions.prompt: 'You have to work' (tú, obligación personal) =
questions.explanation: tener que names the person; tú takes tienes.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué frase es una regla general, sin sujeto concreto?
questions.explanation: hay que states a general rule with no specific subject.

questions.prompt: Completa: Los estudiantes ___ que estudiar cada día. (tener)
questions.explanation: tercera persona plural: tienen.

questions.prompt: Completa: Hay que ir ___ médico si estás enfermo. (contracción a + el)
questions.explanation: a + el contracts to al.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'One has to respect the rules.'
questions.explanation: hay que + infinitivo, with no subject at all.

activities.title: Obligaciones
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Comparing a busy day of personal and general obligations.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: What do you have to do today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Tengo que trabajar y luego tengo que estudiar.
lines.en: I have to work and then I have to study.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Do you have to leave early?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Sí, tengo que salir a las siete. ¿Y tú qué tienes que hacer?
lines.en: Yes, I have to leave at seven. And you, what do you have to do?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Hay que limpiar la casa hoy, así que tengo que estar en casa.
lines.en: The house has to be cleaned today, so I have to be at home.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Entiendo. Hay que hacer esas cosas de vez en cuando.
lines.en: I understand. One has to do those things now and then.

days.title: Los días, los meses y la fecha
days.objective: Name the days of the week and months of the year, and say a date using el + number + de + month.
days.paretoFocus: Dates and days are needed to make any appointment, plan or booking, and Spanish's el lunes vs los lunes distinction changes the meaning.
drills: Say the 7 days of the week in order.
Say the 12 months in order.
Say today's date.

items: Say 'on Monday' versus 'on Mondays'.
Say your birthday month.
Say the date the 3rd of May.

activities.title: Días, meses y fecha
activities.intro: Days and months are lowercase in Spanish. el + day means one specific occurrence; los + day (plural) means every week. Dates use el + number + de + month, with no article before the month.

items.hr: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo
items.en: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday

items.hr: enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio
items.en: January, February, March, April, May, June
items.note: months are lowercase in Spanish

items.hr: julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre
items.en: July, August, September, October, November, December
On Monday I have a meeting.
items.note: el + day: one specific day

items.en: On Mondays I go to the gym.
items.note: los + day (plural): every week

activities.title: Días y fecha
activities.intro: Practise el/los with days and the date pattern.

questions.prompt: 'Every Sunday' =
questions.explanation: los + plural day expresses a repeated occurrence.

questions.prompt: 'This coming Sunday' =
questions.explanation: el + singular day names one specific occurrence.

questions.prompt: Completa: Mi cumpleaños es el tres ___ mayo. (preposición)
questions.explanation: the date pattern is el + number + de + month, no article before the month.

questions.prompt: Completa: El sábado ___ a visitar a mis abuelos. (ir a, yo)
questions.explanation: voy a + infinitivo states a plan.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'On Mondays I go to the gym.'
questions.explanation: los + plural day for a repeated routine.

activities.title: ¿Qué día es la reunión?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Scheduling a meeting and swapping birthdays.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.en: It's on Tuesday. Do you have time?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Los martes trabajo hasta tarde. ¿Puede ser otro día?
lines.en: On Tuesdays I work late. Can it be another day?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Vale, entonces el jueves. ¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños, por cierto?
lines.en: Okay, then Thursday. When is your birthday, by the way?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Es el veinte de julio. ¿Y tu cumpleaños?
lines.en: It's the twentieth of July. And your birthday?

days.title: Decir la hora
days.objective: Tell the time using es la una for one o'clock, son las... for all other hours, and the half/quarter divisions.
days.paretoFocus: Telling time is needed for every appointment, transport schedule and daily routine description.
drills: Say the current time aloud.
Say 3 different times using y media, y cuarto and menos cuarto.
Say what time you have breakfast, lunch and dinner.

items: Say 'it's one o'clock'.
Say 'it's half past three'.
Say 'at eight in the morning'.

activities.title: La hora
activities.intro: One o'clock alone uses es la una because una is singular; every other hour uses son las. Add y + minutes past the hour, or menos + minutes before the next hour, and de la mañana/tarde/noche to specify which part of the day.

items.note: singular es la, because una is one hour
plural son las for every other hour

items.hr: Trabajo de nueve de la mañana a seis de la tarde.
items.en: I work from nine in the morning to six in the evening.

activities.title: ¿Qué hora es?
activities.intro: Practise telling the time.

questions.prompt: 'It's one o'clock' =
questions.explanation: una is the only hour that takes the singular es la.

questions.prompt: 'It's a quarter past four' =
questions.explanation: y cuarto adds fifteen minutes past the hour.

questions.prompt: Completa: Son las ocho ___ cuarto.
questions.explanation: menos + cuarto counts back from the next hour.

questions.prompt: Completa: A las siete de la tarde nos ___ ver la tele juntos. (gustar, singular)
questions.explanation: ver la tele is an infinitive phrase, so gustar stays singular.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'It's half past five in the afternoon.'
questions.explanation: son las + hour + y media + de la tarde.

activities.title: ¿A qué hora quedamos?
activities.intro: Play 'Me'. Arranging a time and place to meet.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: What time shall we meet tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: ¿A las cuatro y media está bien?

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.hr: Perfecto. Yo termino de trabajar a las cuatro menos cuarto.
lines.en: Perfect. I finish work at a quarter to four.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.hr: Genial, entonces quedamos a las cuatro y media en la plaza.
lines.en: Great, so we'll meet at half past four in the square.

lines.speaker: Partner
lines.en: Is it the square near the market?

days.title: En el bar y en la tienda
days.objective: Order and pay in a bar or shop using fixed polite formulas: quiero, ¿cuánto es?, ¿tiene...? and ¿algo más?
days.paretoFocus: This is the single most useful survival scene in the whole course, and it works entirely with structures already known, no imperative required.
drills: Order a drink and a snack using quiero.
Ask if a shop has something using ¿tiene...?
Ask the total price using ¿cuánto es?

items: Order a coffee politely.
Ask if there's anything else to buy.
Ask how much the total is.

activities.title: Pedir y pagar
activities.intro: Quiero + noun is the plain, polite way to order. ¿Tiene...? asks a shop or bar if they have something. ¿Cuánto es? asks the total. ¿Me pone...? is a common way to order in a bar, worth memorizing as a fixed formula rather than a pattern to build other sentences from yet.

items.hr: Quiero un café con leche, por favor.

Could I get a coffee, please?

days.title: Un día cualquiera: repaso de nivel
days.objective: Describe a typical day from morning to night using only the present-tense structures learned so far, consolidating the whole level.
days.paretoFocus: Narrating a full day in the present ties together every structure from the course so far and is exactly the kind of task the level's assessment will ask for.
drills: Describe your whole day from getting up to going to bed, in Spanish.
Include at least one stem-changing verb and one obligation with tener que.
Time yourself describing your day in under two minutes.

items: Name 3 stem-changing verb families.
Say one sentence with hay que.
Say one sentence with gustar.

activities.title: Repaso: un día cualquiera
activities.intro: No new grammar here. This lesson strings together the whole level, present-tense verbs, the four irregular families, ir a, gustar and obligation, into one connected description of a normal day.

items.hr: Hago la cama, desayuno y salgo de casa a las siete.
items.en: I make the bed, have breakfast and leave home at seven.

items.hr: Empiezo a trabajar a las ocho y vuelvo a casa a las seis.
items.en: I start work at eight and get back home at six.

items.hr: Por la tarde tengo que estudiar, pero también me gusta descansar un poco.
items.en: In the afternoon I have to study, but I also like to rest a little.

items.hr: Los fines de semana voy al parque y quedo con amigos.
items.en: At weekends I go to the park and meet up with friends.

items.hr: Por la noche, pienso en el día siguiente.
items.en: At night, I think about the next day.

questions.prompt: 'We have to leave early' =
questions.explanation: tener que names the subject; hay que never takes a personal subject.

questions.prompt: 'I like walking in the park' =
options: Me gusta pasear por el parque
Me gustan pasear por el parque
Yo gusto pasear por el parque
Me gusta pasea por el parque
questions.answer: Me gusta pasear por el parque
questions.explanation: an infinitive as the thing liked always takes the singular gusta.

questions.prompt: Completa: Los sábados ___ al parque con amigos. (ir, yo)
questions.explanation: voy is the irregular yo form of ir.

questions.prompt: Completa: Por la tarde ___ que estudiar un poco. (tener, yo)
questions.explanation: tengo que + infinitivo states a personal obligation.

questions.prompt: Build the Spanish for: 'I start work at eight and get back home at six.'
questions.explanation: empezar stem-changes to empiezo, and volver to vuelvo, in the yo form.
